claims.hypotheses: An invertible operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional space over k has separable reducible characteristic polynomial.
claims.statement: Two complementary nonzero primary spaces put the operator and its full centralizer in the block diagonal Levi.

claims.title: What does one coset contribute to the constant-term integral?
claims.hypotheses: Over a nonarchimedean local field the compactly supported locally constant bi-level-invariant test has zero translated constant terms.
claims.statement: The unipotent sum vanishes. Its common cell volume is the Haar measure of the image of the level lattice under the rectangular change of coordinate.

claims.title: Why does the full local orbital sum vanish?
claims.hypotheses: A local invertible matrix has separable reducible characteristic polynomial. The compactly supported locally constant bi-level-invariant test has zero constant terms on all translates of conjugate proper two-block unipotent groups.
claims.statement: The ordinary local orbital sum vanishes.

claims.title: How does cancellation at one place eliminate an adelic orbital term?

claims.statement: The adelic orbital sum away from p vanishes.

claims.statement: The rational stabilizer of both markings is finite.

claims.title: Which rational elements can contribute on the definite side?
claims.hypotheses: The definite Hecke test has regular support at one split place and cuspidal slices at another. The rational polynomial fails the separable, irreducible, full-degree condition.
claims.statement: Every such definite representative has zero orbital term.

claims.title: Why does the initial Hecke test have zero constant term on every slice?
claims.hypotheses: At a split factor the chosen compact type has open character kernel, finite level index and the property that every smooth irreducible representation containing the type is cuspidal. The splitting and level admit the stated slice factorization.
claims.statement: The normalized character test is idempotent and all its slices have zero constant term. Left convolution by Hecke functions and finite linear combinations preserve the vanishing.
